policy: Generous ceilings on bounded deterministic microbenchmarks plus catastrophic-hang guards for cold starts. Our intent is to catch order-of-magnitude regressions (typically >3-10x) without flaking on host variance. CI must not assert 'faster than an absolute laptop number': the deterministic microbenchmark budgets are the gate; cold-start budgets only catch hangs. The Python executable and Node version are recorded in every report.

budgets.rationale: in-memory content-addressed cache get (structuredClone of a tiny value)
canonicalJson + sha256 over one representative DAG-node key
catastrophic-hang guard; real probe cost varies with installed solvers
catastrophic-hang guard for API+web cold start; host and Next.js build variance dominate
warm in-process GET /health via the governed FastAPI app
catastrophic-hang guard for a real uvicorn cold start to first HTTP 200
queue wait for the tiny in-process participant, from persisted QUEUED to PREPARING
full governed lifecycle with no solver compute; catches orchestration/I-O regressions
governed spawn of a trivial python process (launch path only)
Python ContentCache.get (deepcopy of a tiny tuple)
12-node DAG all-cache-hit pass; the miss delta is reported but not budgeted
committed append-only provenance events per second (catastrophic floor; a 5x contention drop must not flake the gate)
committed native_job_events inserts per second (catastrophic floor under concurrent host load)
sha256 MiB/s on a bounded 4 MiB fixture (catastrophic floor)
catastrophic-hang guard keeping the Python half inside the 60 s suite budget
